svg.text: BEN Engine — Life-Safety One-Line (Hardwired) — Schreiber AI — IFR Rev 2.A · 2026-11-09

HARDWIRED and separate from controls · EPO and HVAC shutdown per NFPA 75 (NFPA 72 detection, NFPA 2001 clean agent) · NEC Art. 645 not invoked (COMPLIANCE.md §0 finding 4) · listed releasing panel · the controls bus only reads dry contacts
2 × 12 V 18 Ah batteries, 24 h standby + 10 min alarm
own 120 V circuit, breaker locked ON, red label
early warning, pipe in return air
supervised initiating circuits, FPLR cable, red
abort: hold to pause 30 s countdown
manual release: dual action, at exit
supervised actuator · nozzles sized for room volume at 5–8 % design concentration
pre-discharge horn, discharge strobe, outside sign
DAMPERS CLOSE · ECONOMIZER CLOSE · IN-ROW FANS OFF
relay to mechanical panel — hardwired, fail-closed dampers
SHUNT TRIPS — UPS output · IT panel · mech. panel
EPO shunt trips; UPS stops output; batteries disconnect (NFPA 75 disconnecting means; Art. 645 not invoked)
doors unlock on alarm for egress (fail-safe), auto-closers hold the agent
BEN NODE X6 'EPO C / EPO NO' + spare DI
reads panel AUX dry contacts: ALARM · TROUBLE · RELEASED · EPO
MONITOR ONLY — cannot open, close or inhibit anything above the line
AUX dry contacts (Form C), unsupervised, to node
ben/<unit>/alarm sev=critical · SMS/e-mail via customer's system
no command path back to the panel exists (by design)
1. Life-safety circuits: FPLR/FPLP red cable, own conduit, no shared boxes.
2. Releasing panel on its own locked-on breaker, not on the controls UPS.
3. The node sees the panel through dry contacts only (dashed line).
4. Test per NFPA 72 ch. 14 yearly; log in docs/MAINTENANCE.md records.
5. Nothing on MQTT / Modbus / SNMP can release agent or trip EPO.
